# scaler_ctrl: generation prompt

*Generated by `ip/scripts/make_ip_prompts.py` from the RTL and testbench sources on 2026-10-16. It follows `ip/docs/MODULE_PROMPT_TEMPLATE.md`; edit any field before use.*

```text
Create a new SystemVerilog IP block for the FPGA Cores 4 U digital IP library.
```

## 1. Identity

- Module name: `scaler_ctrl`
- Library category: `scalers`
- Location: `ip/scalers/scaler_ctrl/`
- One-line purpose: Common control block for all scaler IPs.
- Version: 1.0.0

## 2. Context

- Where it is used: `scaler_anisotropic`, `scaler_bicubic`, `scaler_bilinear`, `scaler_edge_directed`, `scaler_lanczos`, `scaler_mip`, `scaler_nearest`, `scaler_polyphase`, `scaler_trilinear`, `spatial_upscaler`, `video_pipeline`, `video_processor`.
- Existing IP to reuse (do not duplicate):

| Module | From | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `axil_regbus` | `axil_regbus` | AXI4-Lite slave to register bus bridge. |

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Meaning / legal range |
|---|---|---|
| `PIX_W` | `24` | pixel width in bits |
| `ADDR_W` | `14` | AXI-Lite address width |
| `MAX_W` | `1920` | frame buffer width (RO reg) |
| `MAX_H` | `1080` | frame buffer height (RO reg) |
| `IP_ID` | `32'h0` | value of the ID / IP_ID registers |
| `IP_VERSION` | `"1.00"` | VERSION: ASCII "d.dd" of the scaler |
| `IP_DATE` | `32'h0101_2026` | DATE: BCD mm/dd/yyyy of the scaler |
| `CAPS` | `32'h0` | value of the CAPS register |
| `NBUF` | `1` | 1 = single, 2 = double frame buffer |
| `LB_ROWS` | `0` | > 0: line-buffer mode, ring size |
| `LB_TAPS` | `1` | line-buffer mode: vertical taps |
| `LB_CTR` | `0` | window top = int(y) - LB_CTR |
| `LB_RND` | `0` | rounding added to y (16.16) |
| `EXT_WORDS` | `-1` | IP registers at 0x050+ (-1: the IP decodes its own range) |

Reject illegal values at elaboration with `$error` inside a generate block.

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axil_*** - AXI4-Lite slave, address [ADDR_W-1:0], 32-bit data: interface `axil_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`).
- **s_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream slave (input), tdata [PIX_W-1:0], tuser, tlast. tdata = pixel; tready = high only while capturing; tuser = start of frame; tlast = end of line: interface `axis_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Icarus Verilog cannot drive members of interface arrays and Yosys reads interfaces only through sv2v, so keep discrete ports (<prefix>_tdata, <prefix>_awaddr, ...) and put the interface and modport in a comment line directly above each port group: `// s_axis: axis_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24`. Testbenches and Verilator flows may instantiate the interfaces directly.

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

AXI4-Lite / register map: as listed in the behaviour text in section 6. Out-of-range accesses return SLVERR (or DECERR where stated).

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Common control block for all scaler IPs.
* AXI4-Lite slave (axil_regbus) implementing the common registers
* forwards addresses >= 0x040 to the IP-specific ext_* bus
* captures AXI4-Stream frames (tuser = SOF, tlast = EOL) into the
  frame store, dropping data before SOF and flagging errors
* frame sequencing in one of three buffering modes:
    NBUF = 1, LB_ROWS = 0  frame buffer: capture a frame, then generate
                           it; input is stalled while generating
    NBUF = 2, LB_ROWS = 0  double buffer (ping-pong): the next frame is
                           captured into the other buffer while the
                           current one is generated; input only stalls
                           if both buffers are busy
    LB_ROWS > 0            line buffer: the frame store is a ring of
                           LB_ROWS lines; generation starts at SOF and
                           runs concurrently with capture, with row-level
                           flow control in both directions (latency of a
                           few lines). STEP_Y must be >= 0.
  Line-buffer flow control: the IP reports the source y coordinate of the
  next pixel its DDA will emit (lb_nxt_*) and of the pixels already
  emitted but whose rows are not yet read (lb_o_*, lb_a_*). From these the
  block derives
    need(y) = clamp(((y + LB_RND) >>> 16) - LB_CTR + LB_TAPS - 1, 0, H-1)
    top(y)  = clamp(((y + LB_RND) >>> 16) - LB_CTR,               0, H-1)
  lb_hold = 1 while row need(next) has not been fully received, and input
  row r is accepted only while r < top(oldest in-flight pixel) + LB_ROWS.
Common register map (byte offsets, 32-bit):
  0x000 ID        (RO) ASCII IP tag (IP_ID, first character in [31:24])
  0x004 VERSION   (RO) ASCII "d.dd" (IP_VERSION of the scaler)
  0x008 DATE      (RO) BCD mm/dd/yyyy (IP_DATE of the scaler)
  0x00C reserved  (reads 0)
  0x010 CTRL      [0] ENABLE (RW) - run continuously while set
  0x014 STATUS    [0] BUSY [1] FRAME_DONE* [2] SOF_ERR* [3] EOL_ERR*
                  [4] CAPTURING [5] GENERATING   (* = write 1 clears)
  0x018 IN_SIZE   [15:0] width [31:16] height
  0x01C OUT_SIZE  [15:0] width [31:16] height
  0x020 STEP_X    unsigned 16.16 source pixels per output pixel
  0x024 STEP_Y    unsigned 16.16
  0x028 OFFS_X    signed 16.16 source position of output pixel 0
  0x02C OFFS_Y    signed 16.16
  0x030 FRAME_CNT (RO) frames completed
  0x034 IP_ID     (RO) ASCII IP tag (same as ID)
  0x038 CAPS      (RO) IP capability word
  0x03C MAX_SIZE  (RO) [15:0] MAX_W [31:16] MAX_H
  0x050-0x0FF     forwarded to the IP (1-cycle read latency); the IP
                  sees these addresses less 0x10 (0x040-0x0EF, the
                  offsets its own decoder uses), so the ID block
                  does not move its registers internally
  0x100+          forwarded to the IP unchanged (coefficient tables)
Responses: SLVERR for writes to the ID block (0x000-0x00F) and to the
read-only words 0x030-0x03F, and for any access to the unmapped words
0x040-0x04F (0x00C reads 0, OKAY); the access has no effect. With
EXT_WORDS >= 0 the IP has EXT_WORDS registers at 0x050 and up: accesses
beyond them (0x050 + 4 * EXT_WORDS and up, including 0x100+) answer
SLVERR and are not forwarded. EXT_WORDS = -1 (default) forwards the
whole range and always answers OKAY there (the IP decodes it).
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

```text
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   AXI4-Lite register slave (OKAY / SLVERR / DECERR) and AXI4-Stream video input with TUSER =
//   SOF on the first pixel, TLAST = EOL on the last pixel of each line (UG934).
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: SOF / EOL checks (SOF_ERR / EOL_ERR), data before SOF dropped, SLVERR for read-
//   only, ID-block and unmapped words.
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: report the Yosys utilisation; keep it in line with similar library blocks.

Read the file header template from `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt` and start every file you create (RTL, testbench, test tasks, scripts, file lists, Makefile) with that header, filled in: Filename, Author: FPGA Cores 4 U, Description, Date. In RTL the Description is the specification (behaviour, register map, parameters, clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings, latency, resources, errors); in testbenches it says what is checked; test-task files list every task with a one-line description (the test list scripts use it).

Header template file: `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt`   (replace with your own template file if needed)

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for scaler_ctrl.
Checks common register reset values, read/write and RO ID registers;
frame capture (every pixel written once to the right x,y, gen_start
pulses once after the last write, input stalled while generating);
SOF/EOL error detection, re-sync on SOF, W1C sticky status bits;
FRAME_CNT/FRAME_DONE on gen_done, ENABLE loop and return to idle;
forwarding of addresses >= 0x40 to the IP register bus; SLVERR on
writes to the ID block and read-only words and on unmapped words.
Plusargs: +VCD=<file> waveform file, +NO_VCD disables dumping.
The test tasks are in tests/scaler_ctrl_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh scaler_ctrl --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `scaler_ctrl_tb` | `scaler_ctrl_tb` | one test: Self-checking testbench for scaler_ctrl. |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C scalers/scaler_ctrl test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
